INSTALLATION 1. 2. Move the table close to desired location and unlock and raise the table top. While supporting the component door, lift two latches and lower the door. Check that the fuses on the power supply (mounted on the cabinet floor) are securely installed in their fuse clips. (Fuse F4 may be installed but no connections are made to the associated -5 VDC output.) Also check that the 3A line. fuse on the power panel is secure in its clips. Unlock the coin door. Check that the following connectors are firmly seated and that no wires are broken or termination pins loose in the connector. a. Coin door connector. b. Control panel connectors. c. Monitor control 6-pin connector and monitor power connector. d. Transformer connector at the power panel. e. Three connectors on the Power Supply. f. CPU Board connector. g. Speaker connectors. . Check that the twelve socketed IC’s on the CPU Board are firmly seated in their sockets. If it is desired to check or change game adjustments, refer to Game Adjustment procedures which follow. . Insert the line cord through the opening on the floor of the cabinet and pull it to its full extension. . Swing the component door closed and latch it. Close and lock the table top. Reconnect the control panel safety chain and latch the control panel in position. POWER TURN-ON This game MUST BE PLUGGED INTO A PROPERLY GROUNDED OUTLET to PREVENT SHOCK HAZARD and to ensure PROPER GAME OPERATION. DO NOT use a “cheater” plug to defeat the ground pinon the line cord, and DO NOT cut off the ground pin. The line voltage must agree with that specified on the back of the cabinet or serious damage to the machine could occur. For low-line voltage applications (105VAC), refer to the power wiring diagram. 1, Plug the game in and turn it ON. The game should sequence through a self test of certain IC’s on the CPU Board, produce a color pattern, produce a crosshatch pattern, and then come up in the Attract Mode. If the power-up self-test detects a failure, note the failure indication and turn the game OFF and ON. If the failure indication is repeated, replace the faulty IC. Insert coins, press 1- or 2-player start, and play a game to test switches, sound, and program functions. Refer to Tests and Troubleshooting.

GAME OPERATION Direct paint brush using joystick to paint all paths of the maze. Avoid fish who attempt to spoil your paint brush. When pushing the paint roller, paint over the fish and cause a brief return to their aquarium. When selected by an adjust switch setting, a warp hole appears randomly in the maze; escape from the fish by entering the warp hole and return to the start position. Inthe first pattern, a small cat may ‘come out and make tracks on the maze. Paint over the cat and overall its tracks. With the entire maze painted, rain falls and washes off the paint for the succeeding pattern. In subsequent patterns, a mouse, bird, runaway tire, large cat, and an invisible man may come out to make tracks on the maze. Scoring Painting maze - 10 points for unit area. Painting over tracks - 10 points each footprint. Rolling over fish - 50, 100, 200, . . . 3200, 6400, 9000 in first pattern; starts at 100 in second, 200 in third, etc. Painting over cat, mouse, etc. - 1,000. Completing each pattern - 1,000 times pattern number. Bonus paint brush at 10,000 points. GAME ADJUSTMENTS Game adjustments are made using an eight-position DIP switch located in the upper right comer of the CPU board. (Refer to Table 1.) Switches | and 2 control game pricing. Switches 3 and 4 select the number of turns given each player. Switch 5 adjusts game play difficulty. Switch 6 enables and disables the warp hole. Switch 7 defines the game that the CPU board is used with (upright or table). Switch 8 is used to freeze the pattern present on the CRT for monitor adjustments. General Turn the power switch OFF. Use a pen or small screwdriver to make switch settings. ON is toward the rear of the cabinet; OFF toward the front. Game Pricing Switches | and 2 determine game pricing. With switch 1 OFF and switch 2 ON, one game is awarded for one coin (factory recommended setting). With’both switches OFF, one game is awarded for two coins. With switch | ON and switch 2 OFF, two games are awarded for one coin. With both switches ON, free play is in effect. Number of Player Turns Switches 3 and 4 determine the number of piayer tums. The minimum number of turns is three, selected with both switches ON (factory recommended setting). With switch 3 OFF and switch 4 ON, four turns are selected. With switch 3 ON and switch 4 OFF, five turns are selected. With both switches OFF, six turns are selected. ote Pa

Play Difficulty Switch five is used to adjust game difficulty. With switch five OFF, the first pattem is easy. If it is ON (factory recommended setting) the first pattem is made difficult. Warp Hole Switch 6 enables and disables the random warp hole, With it OFF (factory recommended setting), the warp hole is disabled. Set switch 6 to ON to enable it. Upright/Table Games Switch 7 defines the game that the CPU board is used with. For use in an upright version of the game, switch 7 must be ON. For use in a table version of the game, switch 7 must be OFF. Monitor Adjustments Switch 8 is used to freeze the CRT pattern for ease of monitor adjustments such as color convergence, focus, etc. The CRT display is frozen when switch eight is ON. Switch 8 must be turned OFF for normal play of the game. Table 1.
